name: Impact Partners
what: Equity financier for feature-length social issue documentaries, backing around 8-10 projects a year. Filmmakers start with a one-page Letter of Inquiry.
eligibility: Feature docs (generally 50+ min) on an urgent social issue; no fiction, shorts or series. Director and producer attached, one with a completed feature; total budget $300,000-$1.5m. International filmmakers welcome.
next_window: Rolling, no deadline; aims to reply within 4 weeks
notes: LOI via Airtable form on the submit page; no email printed, questions via contact page. Will not screen trailers unless a full proposal is invited.

name: Chicago Media Project
what: Member-funded community of philanthropists and storytellers that pools donations into grants for documentary films and impact campaigns. Reports a total of $10m+ given to 170 films.
eligibility: No public submission route; approach through their network
notes: Site does not describe how filmmakers apply or any deadlines. Also runs the DOC10 festival. Notable links are to the films' distributor pages as listed on CMP's own films page.

name: Artemis Rising Foundation
what: Foundation that finances and supports documentaries on social and environmental issues, working with partner organisations.
eligibility: No open call or public submission route
notes: No email or submission policy on site; appears to work by invitation or partnership. List as a backer to know, not an open fund.

name: Hot Docs Forum
what: Public pitch forum at Hot Docs in Toronto where selected documentary teams pitch to international commissioners and financiers. Includes a rough cut category.
eligibility: Independent production companies. Regular category needs a third-party market trigger (broadcaster, distributor, platform, eligible film board or crowdfunding) and roughly 10-75% of finance in place; max two projects per company. Entry fee CAD $45.
next_window: Hot Docs Industry Conference and Market 26-29 April 2027
notes: Online applications only. Contact email obscured on page; use hotdocs.ca/contact-us.

name: Hot Docs Deal Maker
what: Pre-scheduled one-to-one pitch meetings between documentary teams and buyers or financiers during the Hot Docs market.
eligibility: Any documentary or factual genre from any country: features, TV docs, limited or long-form series. Financing must not be closed. Entry fee CAD $45 per project; selected projects pay registration and need industry passes.
notes: Online only; no post or email submissions.

name: Hot Docs-Slaight Family Fund
what: Funds 3-5 documentaries a year about music artists, with development advances for features and production grants for features and shorts.
amount: Features: no-interest repayable development advance up to CAD $15,000 (max 100% of development budget) or production grant up to CAD $60,000 (max 50% of production budget); shorts: production grant up to CAD $30,000 (max 50% of budget)
eligibility: Three routes: international production companies making films about Canadian musical artists (max 1 a year); Canadian productions, co-productions or treaty productions about Canadian musical artists; or Canadian productions about international musical artists (max 1 a year). Only one project from the two capped routes is considered per cycle. Late rough cut, fine cut or completed projects are not considered.
next_window: Last round closed 11 Dec 2025; next-round details were due late Oct / early Nov 2026 but were not yet posted when checked
notes: A UK company can apply only with a film about a Canadian musical artist. Development advances are repaid when principal photography starts or rights are sold to a third party.

name: Hot Docs Citizen Minutes
what: Commissions six short documentaries (about 6-10 min) on ordinary Canadians improving their communities, with a production lab, Hot Docs premiere and impact campaign.
eligibility: Canadian citizen or PR (co)director with at least one prior credit; up to two projects each; no fiction or completed films.
next_window: Series 4 closed; next series not yet announced
notes: Amount not stated. Email on page is spam-protected so not recorded.

name: Rogers Documentary Fund
what: Private Canadian fund supporting original English and French-language documentary production. Reports a total of $3.26m to 50 projects in 2023.
eligibility: Canadian documentary production; detailed rules in the 2026 guidelines PDFs on the fund page. Apply via the RGF Portal.
next_window: 2027 deadlines not yet announced (2026 had April and August deadlines)
notes: Per-project amounts not stated on the web page.

name: CMF POV Program
what: Selective Canada Media Fund program for one-off point-of-view documentaries in English and French.
eligibility: Canadian productions; criteria in the POV Guidelines and appendices.
next_window: 2027-28 window not yet announced (2026 window ran 28 April-14 May)
notes: Amounts in guidelines, not on page. Email masked on page.

name: Telefilm Canada Theatrical Documentary Program
what: Federal production and post-production financing for Canadian feature documentaries intended for theatrical release, with an Indigenous stream.
eligibility: Canadian production companies headquartered and operating in Canada. Apply via Telefilm's Dialogue portal.
next_window: Next intake not yet announced (2026-27 intake ran 19 March-2 April 2026)
notes: Amounts in guidelines PDF, not on page. Decisions aimed within 80 business days of close.

name: TELUS Fund
what: Funds Canadian content, including documentaries, that improves health and well-being, from development through post-launch audience work.
eligibility: Canadian producers; health and wellness themes. Details in the September 2026 Program Guidelines.
next_window: 2027 Guidelines to be published; no intake dates posted
notes: No amounts or deadlines on site pages; contact via form at telusfund.ca/contact.

name: Doha Film Institute Grants
what: Creative and financial support for feature and short films including documentary, plus creative documentary series grants for MENA talent.
eligibility: Separate MENA and non-MENA criteria by country; features at any stage; documentary series grants for independent MENA screenwriters and producers. Online form only.
notes: Amounts not stated. Fall 2026 cycle ran 22 June-2 July 2026; guidelines at /grants/guidelines.

name: Red Sea Fund
what: Grants for feature documentaries (60+ min) by Arab, African and Asian directors across development, production and post, plus short docs by Saudi directors. Reports a total of $15m to 280+ projects since 2021.
eligibility: Feature docs from Arab, African and Asian directors; shorts (development/production) for Saudi directors only.
next_window: Cycles as published: post-production 6-27 Jan, production 6-21 Mar, development 6-21 May, post-production 6-21 Jul. The page gives no year, so 2027 dates are unconfirmed
notes: Per-grant amounts not stated. The $15m / 280+ projects figure is total support since 2021, not a per-project amount. A reviewer said the dates relate to the 2026 cycle; the official page does not state a year.

name: AFAC Arab Documentary Film Program
org: Arab Fund for Arts and Culture (AFAC)
what: Annual grants for creative documentaries by Arab directors, covering feature development, production and post, and short/medium docs in production and post.
amount: Up to USD 10,000 development; production up to USD 50,000 (feature) / 20,000 (short); post up to USD 25,000 (feature) / 10,000 (short)
eligibility: Arab directors (and producers) in the region or diaspora; non-Arab producer allowed with Arab director. Max two projects per producer per category; online form only.
next_window: 2027 call not yet announced (2026 call opened 2 February)
notes: Page still labelled 'open call' but the 2026 deadline has passed; results announced 31 Aug 2026.

name: CineGouna Funding
what: Development and co-production platform at El Gouna Film Festival for Arab fiction and documentary features, with cash and partner prizes.
amount: US$15,000 each to best development project and best post-production film; total prize money over US$300,000 a year across all awards
eligibility: Arab directors and producers; feature docs in development (before principal photography) or post-production.
next_window: Next call not yet posted (2025 deadlines were July and August)
notes: 2025 deadlines were 15 July (development) and 1 Aug (post). No 2026 call shown; status unclear.

name: Docs by the Sea
what: Annual labs (editing, storytelling, short storytelling, producing) and pitching forum for Asian documentary filmmakers, held in Indonesia.
eligibility: Documentary filmmakers from Asia.
next_window: 2026 edition held 2-9 September; next call not yet announced
notes: No grants or prizes stated; no email on homepage.

name: Asian Network of Documentary (AND) Fund
org: Asian Cinema Fund, Busan International Film Festival
what: Documentary strand of BIFF's Asian Cinema Fund, supporting Korean and Asian documentary projects (six recipients in 2024).
amount: Cash grant up to KRW 20,000,000 per project (around 7 projects)
eligibility: Asian Project category: directors of Asian nationality excluding Korean; Korean Project category: Korean nationality. Projects at any stage from development to post-production.
next_window: 2026 call ran 25 Mar - 20 Apr 2026 (closed); 2027 call not yet announced
notes: Guidelines table is headed 2025 but its dates are for 2026. 2026 selections are listed on the ACF site.

name: Screen Australia Documentary Production
what: Consolidated documentary production funding with three programs: Producer First (replaces the Documentary Producer Program; production or post-production only, no platform commitment needed), Platform First (replaces the Documentary Commissioned Program; needs a confirmed commissioning platform) and Direct-to-Audience (replaces the Online Production Program).
amount: Producer First and Platform First: grant up to AUD $500,000 per project (amounts above that only by exception, as recoupable equity), up to 35% of budgets of $500,000 or less and up to 65% (including Producer Offset) above that; Direct-to-Audience: up to 80% of budget, capped at $300,000, for budgets of $500,000 or less
eligibility: Incorporated company carrying on business in Australia with central management and control there, with an ABN (individual Australian citizens or permanent residents only for Direct-to-Audience); Platform First needs at least a commercial half-hour, a $250,000 per hour minimum budget and all finance confirmed; applicants must discuss the project with an Investment Manager before applying
next_window: Four application rounds per financial year; 2026 deadlines were 16 Apr, 25 Jun and 24 Sep 2026. The next deadline was not shown on the official pages checked
notes: Replaces the separate Producer and Commissioned entries. A reviewer cited a 4 Feb 2027 deadline; it does not appear on the official pages checked. The program page lists 18 June 2026 where the deadlines page lists 25 June 2026. Guidelines revised 8 Oct 2026. An older Screen Australia overview page still shows the retired Producer and Commissioned programs.
max_award: AUD $500,000 grant (more only by exception, as recoupable equity)

name: NZ On Air Scripted and Non-fiction Funding
what: Public funding for New Zealand content including documentary and factual, for local audiences on the platforms they use.
eligibility: Content for a New Zealand audience with a clear plan to reach it on a platform; register on the NZ On Air portal.
next_window: Round Toru opens 10 Dec 2026, closes 28 Jan 2027 (decisions 9 Apr 2027)
notes: Rounds cover scripted and non-fiction together. Amounts not stated.

name: Documentary Australia
what: Not-for-profit that lets approved social-change documentaries receive tax-deductible philanthropic donations via its DGR status, and advises on impact and fundraising.
eligibility: Independent documentaries in focus areas such as environment, health, human rights, women and girls, Indigenous, youth and the arts.
next_window: Check the site for the next round
notes: Only the homepage could be opened; eligibility detail, fees and contact email not verified.
